approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Legal interpretation, evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: AI suitability, proportionality and value hypothesis
canonical_definition: The organization demonstrates that AI is a proportionate mechanism for a defined problem and that expected value is measurable against a technology-neutral baseline, feasible alternatives, total cost, operational burden, human impact and risk.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every proposed AI use, material AI-enabled change and continued AI investment decision, including internally built, externally supplied and embedded AI capabilities.
conditions: Assess the complete socio-technical solution and operating model, not only model performance.
Define the problem, desired outcome and baseline before selecting or defending an AI mechanism.
Compare feasible non-AI, rule-based, process, data and lower-complexity alternatives.
Use decision depth proportionate to lifecycle stage, scale, cost, impact, uncertainty and reversibility.
exclusions: No exclusion is permitted solely because an AI component is inexpensive, already licensed, embedded in a product or labelled experimental.
A narrow maintenance change may rely on a current approved proportionality assessment only when the problem, use, cost, risk and value boundary remain unchanged and this is evidenced.
reassessment_triggers: Material change in problem, users, affected persons, outputs, autonomy, data, model, provider or integration
Value, quality, adoption, cost or risk performance outside approved thresholds
A credible simpler or non-AI alternative becomes available
Pilot-to-production, internal-to-external or low-to-high consequence transition
Control burden, provider cost, energy/resource use or operational dependency materially increases
Continuation or stop criteria expire or are breached

primary_questions.question: Is the problem, desired outcome and measurable value hypothesis defined independently of the AI solution?
Has the chosen AI approach been compared with simpler alternatives and implemented with explicit benefit, cost, risk and operational trade-offs?
Do representative trials and operating evidence demonstrate sufficient value and feasibility to justify progression, with continuation and stop criteria applied?

required_evidence.title: Technology-neutral problem and outcome baseline
required_evidence.claim_supported: The organization has defined the problem, affected process, desired outcome and current baseline independently of a predetermined AI solution.
acceptance_conditions: Defines the current process or decision, users and affected persons, baseline performance, constraints and desired outcome.
Uses language that remains meaningful if AI is removed from the proposed solution.
limitations: A use-case title, vendor proposal or model capability statement does not establish a problem baseline.

required_evidence.title: Measurable value hypothesis and ownership record
required_evidence.claim_supported: Expected benefit is expressed as measurable outcomes with owners, thresholds, time horizons and causal assumptions.
acceptance_conditions: Separates business, user, societal and operational outcomes from activity, usage and model metrics.
Identifies baseline, target, measurement method, owner, decision date and conditions that would falsify the hypothesis.
limitations: Adoption, prompt volume, feature delivery or benchmark improvement alone does not establish realized value.

required_evidence.title: Alternative and proportionality assessment
required_evidence.claim_supported: The selected AI approach has been compared with feasible simpler, non-AI and lower-risk alternatives using explicit decision criteria.
acceptance_conditions: Considers process change, rules, deterministic automation, analytics, data improvement, human service and no-change options where feasible.
Explains why the selected mechanism is proportionate to expected benefit, consequence, uncertainty, cost and control burden.
limitations: A vendor shortlist or comparison between AI models is not a complete alternatives assessment.

required_evidence.title: Total cost and resource baseline
required_evidence.claim_supported: Build, buy, integration, evaluation, security, governance, operations, monitoring, human review, incident and exit costs are identified and bounded.
acceptance_conditions: Includes variable usage, model/provider, data, infrastructure, people, assurance and change costs for the target scale.
Records assumptions, sensitivity ranges, budget owner and cost thresholds.
limitations: Prototype API cost or licence price alone cannot establish total cost of ownership.

required_evidence.title: Risk, impact and control-burden assessment
required_evidence.claim_supported: Expected benefit is evaluated alongside foreseeable harms, uncertainty, dependency, human impact and required governance controls.
acceptance_conditions: Uses the same system, scope, lifecycle and affected-person boundary as the value hypothesis.
Identifies whether required controls or human work materially reduce the proposed benefit or feasibility.
limitations: A generic risk register or low internal risk score does not establish proportionality.

required_evidence.title: Representative comparative trial results
required_evidence.claim_supported: Executed evaluation compares the current AI solution with the approved baseline and relevant alternatives under representative conditions.
acceptance_conditions: Defines versions, samples, users, operating conditions, metrics, thresholds, costs, failures and confidence limitations before interpreting results.
Includes negative, neutral and subgroup results and does not exclude material failure modes.
limitations: A demonstration, benchmark, test plan or selected successful cases cannot establish comparative value.

required_evidence.title: Operational benefit and economics records
required_evidence.claim_supported: Current operation demonstrates whether expected value, cost, quality and human workload are realized within the approved boundary.
acceptance_conditions: Covers representative time periods, user groups, volumes, exception handling, human review, rework and downstream consequences.
Reconciles realized outcomes and costs with the approved value hypothesis and baseline.
limitations: High usage or positive feedback without outcome and cost evidence does not establish realized value.

required_evidence.title: Continuation, stop and requalification decision record
required_evidence.claim_supported: Progression, continuation, constraint or termination follows pre-defined criteria and an attributable decision.
acceptance_conditions: Records evidence considered, threshold result, dissent, conditions, expiry, accountable authority and next reassessment point.
Prevents sunk cost, schedule pressure or technical availability from silently overriding stop criteria.
limitations: A backlog decision, funding renewal or deployment event is not sufficient without the decision basis.

evidence_ceilings: Problem and value documentation can establish DECLARED intent but not comparative feasibility or realized benefit.
Alternative assessment can establish a decision rationale but not technical or operational effectiveness.
Executed trials can establish TESTED comparative evidence only for the assessed versions, populations, conditions and time horizon.
Operational records can establish OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED value only for covered use, cost, quality and impact dimensions.
false_positive_guards: Do not treat the presence of AI as disproportionate solely because a simpler conceptual alternative exists; assess feasibility, outcome and total constraint.
Do not treat a high-cost solution as disproportionate when evidence shows commensurate value and controlled risk.
Do not treat early uncertainty as value theatre when the experiment has explicit falsifiable hypotheses, bounded exposure and enforced stop criteria.
Do not treat low adoption as failure without determining whether adoption is a valid causal requirement for the target outcome.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer value from model quality, user engagement, press visibility, innovation activity or delivery completion alone.
Do not infer proportionality from executive sponsorship, provider reputation or budget approval.
Do not infer that AI is required because the current manual process is weak.
Do not infer production readiness from a successful demonstration or average result that excludes material costs, harms or failure conditions.
contradiction_handling: Conflicting baselines, metric definitions or cost assumptions enforce UNKNOWN until reconciled.
Where business value evidence conflicts with risk, affected-person or operational evidence, preserve both paths and require accountable adjudication.
A positive aggregate result cannot override a material subgroup, safety, rights or hard-gate failure.
freshness_rules: Use the current solution, model/provider version, operating boundary, scale and cost assumptions.
Repeat comparative assessment after material change or threshold breach.
Operational value evidence must cover a representative period and remain within the decision record expiry.

conditions: Block consequential deployment when the problem, value hypothesis or proportionality rationale is materially undefined.
Block progression when representative evidence fails pre-defined minimum value, feasibility or risk thresholds and no formally approved constrained experiment remains.
Constrain operation when benefit, cost or human-impact evidence is materially incomplete for the proposed scale.
Stop or requalify continued use when approved stop criteria are met or the decision record has expired.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: AI RMF Core MAP 1.1, MAP 1.3, MAP 1.5, MAP 2.2, MAP 3.2, MEASURE 1.1 and MANAGE 1.1; NIST AI RMF Playbook MAP 1.3
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Grounds technology-neutral context, organizational goals, risk tolerance, business benefit, go/no-go decisions, measurable performance and prioritization of risk treatment relative to expected value.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Article 9(2)-(7), including targeted risk-management measures and testing against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds appropriate to intended purpose
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Supports lifecycle risk management, targeted and proportionate measures, prior-defined test metrics and evidence-based decisions for high-risk AI systems when the Regulation applies; it does not by itself establish business value.

finding_definitions.title: Problem, desired outcome or value hypothesis is not defined independently of the AI solution
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Prevent consequential progression until a technology-neutral problem, baseline and falsifiable value hypothesis are approved.

finding_definitions.title: Feasible alternatives and proportionality have not been credibly assessed
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain the solution to a bounded experiment or require an accountable alternative and proportionality decision.

finding_definitions.title: Total cost, resource demand, human workload or control burden is materially incomplete
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Do not approve scale or economic claims until material cost and control assumptions are measured and owned.

finding_definitions.title: Representative comparative evidence does not demonstrate sufficient value or feasibility
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block the target transition or continue only within a formally approved learning experiment with explicit limits.

finding_definitions.title: Continuation, stop or value-realization controls are not enforced
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Suspend automatic progression, apply the decision threshold and require requalification or termination as indicated.

machine_may: Extract problem, baseline, alternatives, cost, risk, metric and trial evidence.
Calculate documented comparative metrics and identify missing, conflicting or expired assumptions.
Apply deterministic evidence ceilings and propose eligible conclusion states for human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Select the organization's goals, risk appetite or preferred investment outcome.
Manufacture a value hypothesis from technical capability or retrospective success criteria.
Raise assurance beyond representative evidence or average away a material rights, safety or hard-gate issue.
Override stop criteria, accept residual risk, approve funding, authorize deployment or close a finding.
human_authority_required_for: Approve the problem, value hypothesis, alternatives and proportionality rationale.
Adjudicate material conflicts among value, cost, risk and impact evidence.
Lock findings and approve go, no-go, constrained experiment, continuation, scale or termination decisions.
Accept residual risk and authorize lifecycle transitions.

governance_purpose: Ensure AI investment and use are justified by a specific, measurable and falsifiable value case that remains proportionate to alternatives, total cost, operational burden, human impact and risk.
distinct_claim: A2 owns whether AI is a suitable and proportionate mechanism and whether its value hypothesis is evidenced. A1 owns purpose and use boundaries; D2 owns functional performance; F3 owns residual-risk management; F4 owns authorization; operational financial governance may supply evidence but does not replace the A2 decision.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The underlying problem, affected process or decision and desired outcome are defined independently of AI technology, vendor or model capability.
A current technology-neutral baseline and relevant counterfactual define what improvement must be demonstrated.
The value hypothesis uses outcome measures, owners, thresholds, time horizons and falsification conditions rather than activity or model metrics alone.
Feasible non-AI, deterministic, process, data, human-service and no-change alternatives are compared using explicit criteria.
The selected approach is proportionate after considering benefit, consequence, uncertainty, rights and human impact, total cost, complexity and control burden.
Implementation includes measurable budgets, resource and human-work controls, ownership and traceability for assumptions used in the value case.
Representative comparative trials test the current solution against the approved baseline and alternatives using pre-defined metrics and thresholds.
Continuation, stop, constraint and scale criteria are applied to the complete evidence, including negative, subgroup, cost and risk results.
Operational evidence monitors realized value, cost, quality, human workload and impact and triggers requalification after material deviation or change.
